system.name: VeriSMo
system.one_liner: a formally verified security module for confidential VMs that reasons about memory and lock permissions to guarantee safe concurrent memory access

content.subject: the states a memory range moves through, locked/unlocked, private/shared, trusted/unknown, and which transitions between them are safe

elements.name: Unlocked VMPL0-private
elements.role: VMPL0-private memory not currently locked by any CPU; content trust is unknown (black '?')

elements.name: Locked VMPL0-private
elements.role: VMPL0-private memory locked and verified trusted (green checks both sides); safe for unrestricted access and execution

elements.name: Locked VMPL0-private (Unknown content)
elements.role: VMPL0-private memory that is properly locked/owned (green check) but whose content has not yet been verified (black '?')

elements.name: Unlocked non-private
elements.role: memory shared with the hypervisor or guest OS, not locked; owner is untrusted (devil icon)

elements.name: Locked non-private
elements.role: shared memory locked by the software, permitting copying/writing but not borrowing references; owner still untrusted (devil icon)

elements.name: Memory-Safe Exec codes
elements.role: callout marking that only the fully trusted Locked VMPL0-private state may be treated as memory-safe executable code

elements.name: Lock
elements.role: transition acquiring the lock permission on a memory range

elements.name: Share via PT/RMP updates
elements.role: transition that turns locked private memory into locked non-private (shared) memory via page-table/RMP updates

elements.name: Copy to Private
elements.role: transition that copies locked non-private content into fresh, fully-trusted locked private memory

elements.name: Write
elements.role: transition that turns unknown-content locked private memory into trusted locked private memory by writing verified data

elements.name: Proper PT/RMP updates
elements.role: transition that reclaims locked non-private memory back into locked private memory with unknown content, via legitimate page-table/RMP updates

relations.what: only this trusted state may be treated as memory-safe executable code

content.key_idea: Only memory that is Locked, VMPL0-private and content-verified may be treated as memory-safe; sharing, copying or writing are the sole safe ways to move between the five permission states.
content.reading_order: left-to-right across the top private-memory pair (Unlocked/Locked, then the Unknown-content state via Write), then down to the mirrored non-private pair, linked by Share/Copy transitions

palette.used_for: near-black fill of the '?' unknown-content icons and body text
dark green fill of the checkmark icons marking a trusted/verified state
light gray, used sparingly, likely icon background or padlock body

style.stroke: ~0.5pt outlines; the Unlocked states are drawn with a dashed padlock outline versus solid for Locked states
style.arrows: small triangular direction markers on short connectors between adjacent states, more like pointers than long arrows
style.font: Times New Roman serif, 4-5.5pt, regular weight
style.icons: 12 vector glyph icons: open/closed padlock (sometimes with a key), a circled checkmark, a circled question mark, and a devil face, composed together to badge each state

encoding.color_means: green = verified/trusted (checkmark); black = unknown/unverified (question mark); the devil-face icon marks memory whose owner is an untrusted party (hypervisor or guest OS)
encoding.line_style_means: dashed padlock/state outline marks an Unlocked state; solid marks Locked; plain connecting lines carry the Lock/Unlock/Share/Copy/Write transition labels
encoding.state_means: each of the 5 states is badged by a pair of icons (content-trust glyph + lock glyph) rather than by a colour fill, so trust and lock status are read independently
encoding.marker_means: checkmark = verified, question mark = unverified, devil face = shared with an untrusted owner; these badge icons, not numbers, mark which state a memory range is in
encoding.emphasis: the single green-double-checkmark 'Locked VMPL0-private' state is the only one wired to 'Memory-Safe Exec codes', singling it out as the sole safe-to-execute state
reusable_patterns: small badge-icon pairs (trust glyph + lock glyph) attached to each named state of an access-permission state machine
weaknesses: reusing the same padlock and checkmark glyphs across five states, distinguished only by small colour/fill differences, makes the states easy to confuse without close reading

summary: VeriSMo is a formally verified security module for confidential VMs that reasons about memory and lock permissions to guarantee safe concurrent access. This state-machine figure names five memory states, badged with a lock icon plus a trust icon (a green checkmark, a black question mark, or a devil face): Unlocked/Locked VMPL0-private, a further Locked-VMPL0-private-but-Unknown-content state, and Unlocked/Locked non-private (shared) memory. Lock and Unlock toggle within each privacy class. Crossing classes, 'Share via PT/RMP updates' turns trusted locked-private memory into locked non-private memory, while 'Copy to Private' turns locked non-private memory directly into the trusted private state and 'Proper PT/RMP updates' instead reclaims it as private with content still unknown; a subsequent 'Write' then upgrades that unknown-content state to fully trusted. Only the fully trusted Locked VMPL0-private state is wired to 'Memory-Safe Exec codes', marking it as the sole state safe to execute.
summary_zh: 该图展示VeriSMo的内存状态机：锁形加信任图标（对勾/问号/恶魔）区分私有与共享内存的锁定与可信状态，Share/Copy/Write等操作在其间转换，只有完全可信的Locked VMPL0-private态可执行代码。
notes: states and transition names are read directly from the figure's own labels/icons (checkmark=trusted, '?'=unknown, devil=untrusted owner); the source paragraph is truncated before it fully explains the 'copy' vs 'PT/RMP update' distinction. style.palette falls back to the measured PDF-extracted-SVG attributes since no separate source-SVG histogram was provided.
